harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04): installed aide/aide-common, confirmed the shipped /etc/aide/aide.conf.d/70_aide_etc rule covers /etc with checksums, initialized the database via aideinit, activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db, verified it detects new files under /etc, and confirmed the baseline and daily-check cron job persisted cleanly across a full node restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04.7 Xenial) and confirmed sudo access and aide package availability

Installed aide and aide-common via apt, recovering from a stalled interactive postfix dependency prompt by killing the stuck process, clearing dpkg locks, preseeding debconf answers non-interactively, and reinstalling postfix cleanly
Verified aide.conf.d/70_aide_etc declares /etc as VarDir (checksummed monitoring) with database path /var/lib/aide/aide.db
Ran aideinit to build the initial AIDE database (69,763 entries) and confirmed it was activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db (SHA-256 matched aide.db.new)
Ran aide --check against the baseline and confirmed no /etc discrepancies (only unrelated lxcfs pseudo-files differed)
Created a test file under /etc, re-ran aide --check to prove the baseline flags new /etc content, then removed the test file
Confirmed the aide-common daily cron job (/etc/cron.daily/aide) is installed and cron.service is active/enabled
Captured pre-restart boot_id and aide.db checksum, restarted node1 with a backgrounded shutdown -r now so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec was available again
Verified boot_id changed and uptime reset, confirming a genuine restart occurred
Post-restart, re-verified aide.db checksum unchanged (baseline persisted), cron active, cron.daily/aide present, and a fresh aide --check showed zero /etc-related discrepancies

evidence.requirement: Establish integrity baseline for /etc on node1
evidence.summary: aide.conf.d/70_aide_etc scopes /etc under checksummed monitoring; aideinit built and activated /var/lib/aide/aide.db (69,763 entries) with matching SHA-256 to aide.db.new

evidence.requirement: Baseline detects later changes to /etc files
evidence.summary: aide --check against the fresh baseline showed zero /etc discrepancies; after creating /etc/hosts.aide-test-marker, aide --check flagged it (f++++++++++++++++: /etc/hosts.aide-test-marker), then the file was removed

evidence.requirement: Automated recurring checks are in place
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.daily/aide present (executable, from aide-common) and cron.service enabled/active

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=b185f188-..., uptime-since 10:57:48, aide.db SHA-256, cron active, cron.daily/aide present prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledgement and disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned its ack immediately; the next exec call failed with connection refused, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: exec became available again (pong); boot_id changed to c10c21ec-... and uptime-since reset to 11:03:53, proving a genuine restart; post-restart aide.db SHA-256 unchanged, cron active, cron.daily/aide present, and aide --check showed zero /etc discrepancies, confirming the baseline and monitoring survived recovery
